 Your Des Moines Customers are Here. Where are You? Join our advertising network and connect directly with your local market! Mercedes Saves $60 Million by Replacing Hamilton With Antonelli
 By BVM Sportsdesk, 10/27/2026 Mercedes’ decision to replace Lewis Hamilton with Andrea Kimi Antonelli is paying off on track and on the payroll. Antonelli is reportedly earning a fraction of Hamilton’s former salary while leading teammate George Russell and closing in on the 2026 title. The move gives Mercedes a championship contender and substantial room to redirect money toward the team’s broader needs.
 By the Numbers Antonelli’s reported 2026 pay, including bonuses: about $10 million.
 Hamilton’s reported annual pay at the top of the market: about $70 million.
 Estimated annual salary difference: about $60 million.
 After the U.S. Grand Prix, Antonelli had 365 points to Russell’s roughly 242.
 In 2024, Russell outscored Hamilton 245-223.
 Yes, But The salary comparison is based on reported figures, and Hamilton has shown stronger form in 2026 after struggling in his final Mercedes season. Antonelli’s eventual contract renewal could also raise his price significantly.
 State of Play Antonelli is Mercedes’ clear lead driver and is nearing the 2026 championship.
 Mercedes can use the salary gap to support car development or its finances, subject to cost-cap rules.
 What’s Next As Antonelli’s results strengthen his negotiating position, Mercedes will likely face a more expensive contract discussion. For now, the team retains a title contender on a comparatively modest deal.
 Bottom Line Mercedes appears to have turned a costly driver change into a rare double win: stronger results and a major salary saving. Antonelli’s next contract will test how long the team can keep both advantages.
